text.p: WesterFed Financial Corp. said Wednesday it agreed to acquire intrastate rival Security Bancorp for about $45 million, forming the largest publicly traded banking company in Montana.
The news sent Security's stock soaring $7 to $27.50 on the Nasdaq market in midday trading. WesterFed's stock added 50 cents to $15.75, also on Nasdaq.
WesterFed, which is based in Missoula, is the holding company for Western Federal Savings Bank of Montana and Security Bancorp, based in Billings, is the holding company for Security Bank FSB.
The combined company will have total assets approaching $1 billion, total deposits of $640 million and 35 offices in 20 communities throughout Montana.

Under the terms of the agreement, Security Bancorp shareholders may opt to receive either $30 in cash for each of their shares, swap their stock for WesterFed shares or may choose to receive cash and stock as long as the stock portion is 40 to 45 percent of the deal.
The exchange ratio will depend on the average closing price of WesterFed stock for the 20 trading days beginning 30 trading days prior to the closing of the deal.
Based on WesterFed's stock price of $15.75 on Wednesday, and excluding stock options, the merger would have a value of about $45.4 million, WesterFed said.
WesterFed said the deal was expected to add to earnings in the first full fiscal year of combined operations, assuming only modest cost reductions.
